headline: Sensex drops nearly 400 points as crude oil surges past $102 and global markets weaken

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Crude oil prices surged above $102 per barrel following UN remarks by Iran's president.
Global bond selloff and rising US Treasury yields weighed on broader Asian equities.
Financial and insurance stocks faced heavy selling pressure due to an IRDAI proposal.
US Dollar jumped to near a two-month high, adding pressure on Indian benchmark indices.
whatHappening: Sensex dropped nearly 400 points while Nifty and GIFT Nifty extended weakness at open.
Macquarie initiated coverage on NSE and BSE with 'Outperform' ratings ahead of NSE's listing.
Jefferies issued a 'Buy' call on Vishal Mega Mart citing a 54% upside potential.
Whirlpool of India featured among key stocks displaying an upward trending RSI indicator.
summary: Indian stock benchmarks opened sharply lower today as Sensex dropped nearly 400 points amid crude oil crossing $102 per barrel. Rising US Treasury yields, a strong US dollar, and IRDAI proposal fears led to selloffs in financial and insurance shares. Meanwhile, exchange stocks NSE and BSE attracted positive coverage from Macquarie ahead of NSE's upcoming IPO listing.
